entries.text: For November 2026, we welcome Johannes Maron as our DSF member of the month! ⭐ Johannes has long been part of the Django community. He is a frequent contributor including project such as django-hijack which has more than 1.7K stars! He is part of the Django Review and Triage team. He is a DSF member since September 2025. You can learn more about Johannes by visiting Johannes' website and his GitHub Profile. Let’s spend some time getting to know Johannes better! Can you tell us a little about yourself? (hobbies, education, etc) Johannes Maron, or joe, born Johannes Hoppe in the GDR. Raised in West Germany only to return to his home state for uni. Studied software engineering at the Hasso-Plattner institute, dropped out and lived the start-up life. I still live in Potsdam and have the most amazing pug, son and wife (in alphabetical order). I have an idea but where your nickname "codingjoe" comes from? I am joe, and I code. Honestly, I was young, and I am just happy it's not naughtyb0i420 and thus never changed it. How did you start using Django? I started using Django for my very first company, I believe it was version 1.3? I have used it for every company I build ever since, and would always do it again. What other framework do you know and if there is anything you would like to have in Django if you had magical powers? Who said I don't have magic powers? entries.summary: We are pleased to announce that the 2026 Malcolm Tredinnick Memorial Prize has been awarded to Raffaella Suardini!
entries.text: We are pleased to announce that the 2026 Malcolm Tredinnick Memorial Prize has been awarded to Raffaella Suardini! Raffaella embodies the values that define the Django community: generosity, respect, thoughtfulness, and a deep commitment to supporting others. She is a tireless community leader who creates spaces where newcomers thrive ❤️, exactly in the spirit of our prize and Malcolm Tredinnick’s work. About Raffaella As an admin of Djangonaut Space, Raffaella helps make the program a welcoming place for new contributors. She writes session announcements, keeps Djangonauts informed and connected, and speaks about building inclusive open-source communities, including at FOSDEM 2025. Beyond Djangonaut Space, Raffaella is an organizer of PyCon Italia, a Django Girls+ coach where she mentors people new to Django, and an individual member of the Django Software Foundation. What people said about Raffaella’s involvement in the community: As a long-time Djangonaut Space admin and session organizer, she celebrates everybody’s wins with authentic enthusiasm and amplifies the visibility of the Djangonauts on social media. Raffaella is really interested in the Djangonauts as a whole, and she has a talent for connecting people with similar interests. She shares stories from her own experience that people can relate to; one of them made me feel at home in the Django community. She also takes a genuine interest in people’s Django contribution successes beyond the program and keeps support

entries.summary: The Django Software Foundation is inviting nominations for its 2027 Board of Directors. Five of the seven Board positions are open for election this year.
entries.text: The Django Software Foundation is inviting nominations for its 2027 Board of Directors. Five of the seven Board positions are open for election this year. The Board of Directors play a central role in the Foundation's work, overseeing its governance, fundraising, marketing, and outreach, and supporting Django events and initiatives across the globe. Directors serve staggered two-year terms. Nominations are open to all. You do not need to be a DSF member or have previous Board experience to apply. We welcome applications from anyone interested in contributing to the Foundation and the future of Django. An interesting time to join This is a particularly interesting year to join the Board. For the first time in 21 years, the Foundation is hiring an Executive Director. Joining the Board means being part of this important governance transition, alongside the opportunity to shape and contribute to the DSF’s initiatives. We look forward to receiving applications from a diverse range of backgrounds and experiences. Thank you A special thank you to Jacob Kaplan-Moss for his guidance and contributions during his time on the Board. Jacob has decided to step down after completing one year of his term. We also thank Jeff Triplett, Abigail Gbadago, Paolo Melchiorre, and Tom Carrick for the time, dedication, and effort they have invested in the Foundation as they complete their two-year terms. entries.summary: In accordance with our security release policy, the Django team is issuing releases for Django 6.1.3, Django 6.0.10, and Django 5.2.19.
entries.text: In accordance with our security release policy, the Django team is issuing releases for Django 6.1.3, Django 6.0.10, and Django 5.2.19. These releases address the security issues detailed below. We encourage all users of Django to upgrade as soon as possible. CVE-2026-108147: Potential memory exhaustion in MultiPartParser via base64-encoded file upload When using django.http.multipartparser.MultiPartParser, multipart uploads with Content-Transfer-Encoding: base64 could be buffered entirely in memory, regardless of FILE_UPLOAD_MAX_MEMORY_SIZE, before being passed to upload handlers, potentially consuming excessive memory. This issue has severity "low" according to the Django Security Policy. Thanks to Ignacy Kujawa for the report. CVE-2026-111211: Potential log injection via unescaped geometry form values django.contrib.gis.forms.GeometryField and its widgets logged invalid submitted values directly, allowing control characters (e.g. newlines or ANSI escape sequences) to be written unescaped into logs. This could enable log injection or forgery, letting attackers manipulate log appearance or structure, especially in logs processed by external systems or viewed in terminals. This issue has severity "low" according to the Django Security Policy. Thanks to Aaron chen for the report. entries.summary: After more than three years as a Django Fellow, I will be taking a three-month break from Fellow duties during November, December, and January.
entries.text: After more than three years as a Django Fellow, I will be taking a three-month break from Fellow duties during November, December, and January. This time will allow me to properly rest, reset, and recover from some accumulated fatigue so I can return with renewed energy. I'm deeply grateful to the DSF Board for its support of this arrangement, and to my Django Fellow colleagues and the members of the various teams and working groups who will help provide continuity during my leave. I look forward to resuming my Fellow duties in February. Super excited to be release manager for Django 2028!
entries.title: Natalia Bidart - Planned short-term leave

entries.summary: Hi Django community, thank you all for continuing to contribute to Django. The Steering Council is reaching out to bring people's attention to a few areas.
entries.text: Hi Django community, thank you all for continuing to contribute to Django. The Steering Council is reaching out to bring people's attention to a few areas. We have major features we'd like to test and review for 6.2, smaller changes that could use attention and then various New Feature ideas we'd like community input on. Major features These PRs are things we'd like to refine, test and get merged in. We're looking for people to test the features themselves and review the PRs. Please see our guidelines on reviewing PRs. CompositeField (multi-column subqueries) (this only needs testing, not review.) DEFAULT_PK_FIELD setting (e.g. UUID primary keys) Move models between apps Sage Abdullah has a great Django London talk on how to test your project against Django's main branch. Please note that you would need to change the branch to point to the PR’s specific branch. Other features These are other PRs that we thought would be cool to have included in 6.2. They are in various states of refinement. We're looking for people to test and review the PRs. They are smaller in nature, so it may be easier to get involved here. Adding QuerySet.executed_queries Partitioned cookies Support for the HTTP QUERY method Improve CSRF debug messaging behind proxies New Features This section is bringing attention to the New Features queue. entries.text: We are no longer accepting new security reports for the Django project through HackerOne. Existing reports submitted through HackerOne will remain open and continue to be handled by the Django Security Team. If you discover a security issue in Django, please follow the reporting process described in the Django security policies. Security issues should be reported by emailing security@djangoproject.com

entries.summary: In accordance with our security release policy, the Django team is issuing releases for Django 6.1.2, Django 6.0.9, and Django 5.2.18.
entries.text: In accordance with our security release policy, the Django team is issuing releases for Django 6.1.2, Django 6.0.9, and Django 5.2.18. These releases address the security issues detailed below. We encourage all users of Django to upgrade as soon as possible. CVE-2026-77050: Potential denial-of-service vulnerability in get_supported_language_variant() django.utils.translation.get_supported_language_variant() was subject to a potential denial-of-service attack when processing many distinct, very long language codes. Language codes were used as keys in an in-memory cache before their length was limited, potentially consuming excessive process memory. To mitigate this vulnerability, language codes longer than 500 characters are now rejected or truncated before the cached lookup. This issue has severity "low" according to the Django security policy. Thanks to Gleb Lizunov for the report. CVE-2026-84429: Potential denial-of-service vulnerability in HTTP header parsing django.utils.http.parse_header_parameters() was subject to a potential denial-of-service attack due to quadratic time complexity when parsing a value with many separators inside a quoted parameter. An unauthenticated request could reach this parsing through headers such as Accept or Content-Type, for instance via the content negotiation performed by HttpRequest.accepts(). entries.summary: Hello Everyone 👋 It is that time of year again when we recognize someone from our community in memory of our friend Malcolm.
entries.text: Hello Everyone 👋 It is that time of year again when we recognize someone from our community in memory of our friend Malcolm. Malcolm was an early core contributor to Django and had a huge influence on the Django we know today. Besides being knowledgeable, he was also especially friendly to new users and contributors. He exemplified what it means to be an amazing Open Source contributor. We still miss him to this day. The prize Our prizes page summarizes it nicely: The Malcolm Tredinnick Memorial Prize is a monetary prize, awarded annually, to the person who best exemplifies the spirit of Malcolm’s work - someone who welcomes, supports, and nurtures newcomers; freely gives feedback and assistance to others, and helps to grow the community. The hope is that the recipient of the award will use the award stipend as a contribution to travel to a community event -- a DjangoCon, a PyCon, a sprint -- and continue in Malcolm’s footsteps. Please make your nominations using our form: 2026 Malcolm Tredinnick Memorial Prize nominations. Django Software Foundation board members, Django Fellows, and the Treasurer’s assistant are not eligible to receive the prize. You are still welcome to use the appreciation field below to recognize them, and we’ll make sure those messages are passed along. UPDATED: We will take nominations until Friday, October 16th, 2026, Anywhere on Earth, and will announce the results in late October. entries.summary: For September 2026, we welcome Ken Whitesell as our DSF member of the month!
entries.text: For September 2026, we welcome Ken Whitesell as our DSF member of the month! ⭐ Ken has long been part of the Django community, serving for many years as an helper in the Django forum and recipient of the Malcolm Tredinnick Memorial award. He has been a volunteer for DjangoCon US for over ten years. He is a DSF member since September 2017! You can learn more about Ken by visiting Ken's blog and his GitHub Profile. Let’s spend some time getting to know Ken better! Can you tell us a little about yourself? (hobbies, education, etc) Hi everyone! I've been retired for a little more than a year now. After 45 years working in software development, I'm now free to spend my time working on what interests me. (You could say that what used to be my hobby is now my profession.) I'm currently living in the mountains about 60 miles south-east of Pittsburgh. I mostly consider myself a boardgamer. Boardgaming has been a serious hobby for me for more than 50 years now, and has been one of the driving forces in my personal development as a programmer. Not in terms of programming or developing games, but doing analysis. I enjoy looking at the probabilities and patterns that may exist in particular games. To a lesser extent, I'm starting to develop an interest in using AI to create computer opponents. My education was primarily informal.
